source_lines.text: abbad@abbad, abbod, abbud, abbot, es; m: abboda, an; m. I. an abbot; abbās, -- the title of the male superior of certain religious establishments. In point of dignity an abbot is generally next to a bishop :-- Se ārwurða abbad Albīnus the reverend abbot Albinus, Bd. pref. II. bishops were sometimes subject to an abbot, as they were to the abbots of Iona :-- Nū, sceal beōn ǣfre on Iī abbod, and nā biscop now, in Iī, there must ever be an abbot, not a bishop, Chr. 565; Th. 32, 10-16, col. l. [Laym. abbed: O. Frs. abbete.] DER. abbad-dōm, -hād, -isse, -rīce: abboda.@abbad

senses.gloss_en: bishops were sometimes subject to an abbot, as they were to the abbots of Iona

source_lines.text: abbudhad@abbud-hād, es; m. The state or dignity of an abbot; abbatis dignitas :-- Munuchād and abbudhād ne syndon getealde to ðysum getele monkhood and abbothood are not reckoned in this number, L. Ælf. C. 18; Th. ii. 348, 31.@abbud-had

senses.gloss_en: The state or dignity of an abbot

source_lines.text: abaedan@ā-bǣdan. Substitute the following: I. to force, wring :-- Ele ābǣdan and āwringan of þām bergum ab olivis exigere oleum torquendo, Gr. D. 250, 22. II. to compel:-- Gif ðæt nȳd ābǣdeþ cum exhiberi mysterium ipsa necessitas compellit, Bd. l, 27; S. 497, 1. III. to demand, require. (l) where the object is something needed :-- Nāniges fultumes ābǣdeþ siō lār nullum adjutorium expostulet ratio, Nar. 2, 2.@a-bædan
abitweonum@a-bitweōnum; prep. Between; inter :-- Sēt him a-bitweōnum he sat between them.@a-bi-tweonum,a-bitweonum
abitweonum@a-bitweōnum. Dele.@a-bi-tweonum,a-bitweonum

adon@a-dōn; p. -dyde; impert. -dō; v. a. To take away, remove, banish; tollere, ejicere :-- Ne māgon ðē nū heonan adōn hyrste ða reādan the red ornaments may not now take thee hence, Exon. 99a; Th. 370, 14; Seel. 57. Adō ða buteran remove the butter, L. M. 1, 36; Lchdm. ii. 86, 22. Adō of ða buteran take off the butter, 86, 19.@a-don

adon@ā-dōn. Dele Ælfc. T. 5, 25: Gen. 7, 23: 9, 11, and add: with words further marking removal, (1) fram:--Ic ādyde (abstuli) hosp fram eōwrum cynne, Jos. 5, 9. Ādoo from ðē ðā byrðenne, Past. 225, 11. (2) of:--Hē ādēð eōw of ðisse worulde, Bt. 19; F. 70, 17.@a-don
adon@ā-dōn. Add: -- Hungor ādyde hī. Chr. 1086. Ādōþ gatu tollite portas, Ps. Rdr. 23, J.@a-don

senses.gloss_en: and add: with words further marking removal

source_lines.text: abisgung@ā-bisgung e; f. Substitute the following for ā-bysgung in Dict. I. occupation, employment, business. v. ā-bisgian, I :-- For ðǣre ūterran ābisgunge . . . for ðǣre ābisgunge ðāra ūterra weorca in exteriorum occupatione. Past. 127, 9, 12. II. trouble, disturbance. v. ā-bisgian, II :-- Hit is cūð ðætte siō ūterre ābisgung ðissa worold-ðinga ðæs monnes mōd gedrēfð and hine scofett hidres ðædres constet, quod cor externis occupationum tumultibus impulsum a semetipso corruat. Past. 169, 12.@a-bisgung
a@ā, aa, aaa; adv. Always, ever, for ever; hence the O. Eng. AYE, ever; semper, unquam, usque :-- Ac ā sceal ðæt wiðerwearde gemetgian but ever must the contrary moderate. Bt. 21; Fox 74, 19.@a,-a,a-

senses.gloss_en: Always, ever, for ever; O. Eng; ever

source_lines.text: a@a; prep. acc. To, for; in :-- A worlda world to or in an age of ages; in seculorum seculum, Ps. Th. 18, 8.@a,-a,a-
aad@aad a pile :-- He mycelne aad gesomnode he gathered a great pile, Bd. 3, 16; S. 542, 22. v. ād.@aad

abacan@a-bacan, ic -bace, ðū -bæcest, -bæcst, he -bæceþ, -bæcþ, pl. -bacaþ; p. -bōc, pl. -bōcon; pp. -bacen To bake; pinsere, coquere :-- Se hlāf þurh fȳres hǣtan abacen the bread baked by the heat of fire. Homl. Pasc. Daye, A. D, 1567, p. 30, 8.@a-bacan
abacan@a-bacan to bake:-- Nim ælces cynnes melo and ābacæ man hlāf, Lch. i. 404, 5. Þost tō cicle ābacen, 364, 15: Gr. D. 87, 21.@a-bacan

abbadisse@abbadisse, abbodisse, abbatisse, abbudisse, abedisse, an; f. [abbad an abbot, isse a female termination, q. v.] An abbess; abbatissa :-- Riht is ðæt abbadissan fæste on mynstrum wunian it is right that abbesses dwell closely in their nunneries, L. I. P. 13; Th. ii. 320, 30.@abbadisse
abbodrice@abbod-rīce, abbot-rīce, es; n. The rule of an abbot, an abbacy; abbatia :-- On his tīme wæx ðæt abbodrīce swīðe rīce in his time the abbacy waxed very rich, Chr. 656; Ing. 41, l.@abbod-rice

senses.gloss_en: The rule of an abbot, an abbacy

source_lines.text: abelgan@a-belgan, ic -beige, ðū -bilgst, -bilhst, he -bylgþ, -bilhþ, pl. -belgaþ; p. -bealg, -bealh, pl. -bulgon; pp. -bolgen, v. trans. [a, belgan to irritate] To cause any one to swell with anger, to anger, irritate, vex, incense; ira aliquem tumefacere, irritare, exasperare, incendere :-- Ne sceal ic ðē abelgan I would not anger thee, Salm. Kmbl. 657; Sal. 328.@a-belgan

senses.gloss_en: To cause any one to swell with anger, to anger, irritate, vex, incense

source_lines.text: aberan@a-beran; p. -bær; pp. -boren. I. to bear, carry, suffer; portare, ferre :-- Ðe man aberan ne mæg which they are not able to bear, Mt. Bos. 23, 4. II. to take or carry away; tollere, auferre :-- Abær hine of eowdum sceāpa sustulit eam de gregibus ovium, Ps. Spl. 77, 76. v. beran.@a-beran
ablisian@a-blīsian; p. ode; pp. od To blush; erubescere :-- Oðð eōwre lyðere mōdd ablīsige donec erubescat incircumcisa mens eorum. Lev. 26, 41.@a-blisian

abarian@a-barian; . p. ede; pp. ed [a, barian to make bare; bær, se bara; adj. bare] To make bare, to manifest, discover, disclose; denudare, prodere, in medium proferre :-- Gif ðū abarast ūre sprǣce si sermonem nostrum profers in medium, Jos. 2, 20.@a-barian

abarian@ā-barian. Add: I. to make bare, strip :-- Stōwe rōde ābarude locum cruce denudatum, Angl. xiii. 427, 894. II. to lay bare, expose, disclose:-- Ælfremeda wunda nā ābarian (detegere) and geswutelian, R. Ben. I. 80, 12.@a-barian

senses.gloss_en: To make bare, to manifest, discover, disclose

source_lines.text: abedan@a-beden asked, Nicod. 12; Thw. 6, 15: Bd. 4, 10; S. 578, 31; pp. of a-biddan.@a-beden
abeofian@a-beofian To be moved or shaken, to tremble; moveri, contremere :-- Ealle abeofedan eorðian staðalas movebuntur omnia fundamenta terrae, Ps. Th. 81, 5. v. beofian.@a-beofian

senses.gloss_en: To be moved or shaken, to tremble

source_lines.text: abecede@ābēcēdē; f. An ABC, alphabet:-- Seō forme ābēcēdē on ðām gerīme ys bītan pricon.@a-becede

abaligan@a-bæligan; p. ode; pp. od To offend, to make angry; irritare, offendere :-- Sceal gehycgan hæleða ǣghwylc þæt he ne abælige bearn waldendes every man must be mindful that he offend not the son of the powerful, Cd. 217; Th. 276, 27; Sat. 195. v. a-belgan, a-bylgan.@a-bæligan
abeatan@a-beātan; p. -beōt; pp. -beāten To beat, strike; tundere, percellere :-- Stormum abeātne beaten by storms, Exon. 21b; Th. 58, 26; Cri. 941. v. beātan.@a-beatan

abisgian@ā-bisgian, -bysgian; p. ode; pp. od; v. a. To occupy, employ, keep busy; occupare :-- Hī wurdon ābysgode mid ðǣm woroldlīcum þingum they were kept busy with worldly things, Past. 127, 9. Ābysgad occupatus, Wrt. Voc. ii. 51, 25.@a-bisgian
aslacian@ā-slacian; p. ode To slacken; remittere :-- Nānum ne geyfelode ne āslacude, Bd. 4, 18; Sch. 437, 1.@a-slacian

aslacian@ā-slacian. Add: I. to slacken, become slack, (l) physical :-- Bid dæs mannes wæstm gebīged, his swura āslacod. Hml. Th. i. 614, 13. II. to make slack :-- Āslacudæ, āsclacade hebitavit, Txts. 66, 491.@a-slacian
awundrian@ā-wundrian. Substitute: I. to wonder, be astonished:-- Ic āwundrode mirabar, Gr. D. 244, 13. II. to wonder at, admire, magnify:-- Āuundradon God magnificabant Deum, Lk. L. 5, 26.@a-wundrian

bletsian@bletsian, bletsigan; part. bletsiende, bletsigende; p. ode, ade; pp. od, ad; v. a. To BLESS, wish happiness, consecrate; benedicere, consecrare :-- Ic Ismael ēstum wille bletsian I will bless Ishmael with favours, Cd. 107; Th. 142, 5; Gen. 2357.@bletsian

bletsian@bletsian (from blēdsian, bloedsian). Add: I. to hallow, consecrate :-- Genom se Hǣlend hlāf and bletsade, Mt. R. 26, 26. II. to call holy, adore :-- Mec giē bledtsiges, Jn. L. 13, 13. III. to invoke divine favour upon :-- Þæt ic þē bletsige, Gen. 27, 4. IV. to speak gratefully of a person :-- Eal rihtgelȳfed folc sceal hine bletsian, Bl. H. 167, 14.@bletsian
abeornan@a-beornan; p. -bearn, -barn, pl. -burnon; pp. -bornen, v. intrans. To burn; exardere :-- Fyr abarn exarsit ignis, Ps. Th. 105, 16. v. beornan.@a-beornan

abeornan@ā-beornan (-bi(e)rnan). Add: :-- Ābyrnð exardescit, Ps. L. 38, 4. Hē ābarn (exarsit) mid ðȳ bryne wælhreōwnesse, Gr. D. 162, 22. Ðæt his mōd āburne (exardesceret), 337, 33. Āburnon exarserunt, Ps. L. 117, 12.@a-beornan
drugung@drugung, e; f. A dryness, a dry place; siccĭtas, inăquōsus lŏcus :-- Hī costadon God in drugunge temtāvērunt Deum in siccĭtāte, Ps. Surt. 105, 14.@drugung
gar@gār; m. A spear; hasta :-- Gār oft þurhwōd fǣges feorhhūs, By. 296.@gar

gar@gār. Add; I. a weapon with a pointed head. (1) where the use is uncertain :-- Gār oft þurhwōd fǣges feorhhūs, By. 296. II. the head of a weapon :-- Gār sceal on sceafte, ecg on sweorde, Gn. Ex. 203.@gar

senses.gloss_en: a weapon with a pointed head

source_lines.text: adloma@ād-loma, -lama? an; m. One crippled by the flame? cui flamma claudicationem attulit? -- Earme ādloman poor wretches, i.e. diaboli, Exon. 46a; Th. 156, 33; Gū. 884.@ad-loma
